title: Multi-window state propagation and management-event timing
purpose: Propagate the qualified per-window direct active-set solution through multiple coupling windows and quantify timestep-partition effects against an independent continuous-time event reference.

discrete_contract.commit: h_(n+1) = solved end level; no tentative state leaks across windows
discrete_contract.shortage_feedback: none; request rate is exogenous and does not carry backlog
discrete_contract.cumulative_balance: A*(h_0-h_N) = sum(U_n) + sum(V_n), positive V is Basin-to-groundwater exchange

continuous_reference.domain: constant A,C,hgw, request rate r; hgw<hmin<h0; no external inflow; one irreversible management shutoff event
continuous_reference.hit_time: t_hit=-(A/C)*ln((hmin-h_eq)/(h0-h_eq)) when full solution reaches hmin

experiments.P1: multi-window propagation uses each accepted end level as the next start level and closes every window plus the cumulative water balance
experiments.P2: in a nonbinding FULL regime, N equal discrete windows reproduce the independently derived trapezoidal recurrence h_N=h_eq+g^N(h0-h_eq), g=(1-k/2)/(1+k/2)
experiments.P3: canonical event case reproduces the preregistered one-window and two-half-window allocations exactly
experiments.P4: for N=16,32,64,128 equal windows, final-level and cumulative-delivery errors decrease monotonically toward the independent continuous event solution
experiments.P5: the coarse one-window solution underdelivers management water and ends artificially at hmin relative to the continuous event reference
experiments.P6: with sufficiently fine partitioning, a later ZERO-demand window can physically move Basin level below hmin, confirming hmin is a management threshold rather than a physical floor
experiments.P7: per-window requested volume remains request_rate*dt after prior shortage; no hidden shortage backlog is introduced
experiments.P8: cumulative mass balance remains closed for all tested partitions even though cumulative delivery and exchange are partition dependent

interpretation_rules: partition dependence is a temporal-discretization/decision-timing effect, not automatically a water-balance error
continuous reference is restricted to the preregistered constant-parameter one-event domain
management threshold may be crossed by physical hydrology after managed delivery reaches zero
no demand carryover or behavioral SWAP feedback is introduced in DUMMY-08
no production coupling timestep is prescribed
forbidden: no backlog or adaptive demand rule
no claim that the continuous one-event reference covers networks or varying groundwater heads
no empirical acceptance tolerance used to tune timestep
